channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: UN experts report finding reasonable grounds to believe U.S. war crimes occurred in Iran.
item.description: A UN fact-finding mission reported "reasonable grounds" that U.S. missile strikes on a school and sports complex in Iran resulted in the deaths of up to 177 civilians. Western outlets frame the report as a balanced legal inquiry, highlighting both U.S. war crimes and Iranian crimes against humanity. Conversely, Middle Eastern reporting focuses on the human cost and specific technical failures, framing the strikes as a deliberate or negligent disregard for civilian life.

item.title: United States approves sale of up to 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The United States has notified Congress of its intent to sell up to 48 F-35 fighter jets and related equipment to Saudi Arabia in a deal valued at approximately $24.3 billion. While all sources confirm the technical details and figures, coverage differs regarding the primary motivation for the sale. Middle Eastern outlets frame the deal as a critical response to regional missile threats and a milestone for Arab defense, whereas Western reporting focuses on internal U.S. debates over technology security.

item.title: United States issues visas for Iranian officials to attend United Nations meetings in New York
item.description: The United States granted visas to high-level Iranian officials, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, for the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Western outlets frame the decision as a pragmatic diplomatic compromise, emphasizing the specific travel restrictions and purchasing prohibitions placed on the delegation. In contrast, Russian reporting focuses on the high-ranking status of the attendees, framing the event as a significant interaction between the U.S. and the Iranian regime.

item.title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi sentenced to 25 years for war crimes in The Hague
item.description: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague sentenced former President Hashim Thaçi and three other KLA leaders to 25 years in prison for war crimes committed during the 1998-1999 conflict. Western outlets frame the verdict as a domestic crisis, emphasizing local outrage and the perceived injustice felt by the Kosovar community. Conversely, Russian reporting frames the conviction as a geopolitical issue, highlighting the role of NATO-backed actions and the broader international involvement in the conflict.

item.title: United States denies Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend a United Nations summit.
item.description: The United States denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend the United Nations assembly in New York for the second consecutive year. While both Western and Russian outlets confirm the denial and the resulting remote participation, they differ significantly in their framing of the motive. Western reports frame the decision as a pragmatic tool to enforce accountability for a lack of peace reforms, whereas Russian reports frame it as a deliberate act of diplomatic obstruction and a challenge to international cooperation.

item.title: Multiple casualties reported following strikes and a reported aircraft shootdown in the Yemen conflict.
item.description: On September 17, 2026, a Saudi F-15 fighter jet was reportedly shot down over Marib, and strikes occurred in the Taiz and Hajjah provinces. Western outlets focus on the Houthis' advanced military capabilities and the specific humanitarian impact on civilian casualties. In contrast, Russian sources emphasize the scale of the Saudi aerial campaign and the retaliatory strikes launched by Houthi forces against Saudi infrastructure.

item.title: European Union officials support a proposal for Canada to become an associate member state.
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed a new "associate member" status for Canada to enhance cooperation in defense, energy, and technology. While all outlets report the proposal as a move toward a "unique alliance," coverage diverges on the primary motivation. Western sources frame the move as a proactive step for shared values and economic security, while Eastern and other international outlets emphasize the move as a defensive maneuver against American pressure and shifting trade dynamics.

item.title: Russia and China veto United Nations resolution regarding monitoring of sanctions against Iran
item.description: Russia and China vetoed a U.S.-backed United Nations Security Council resolution intended to extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts monitoring sanctions against Iran. While all sources confirm the veto occurred, coverage differs significantly in framing the motivations behind the move. Middle Eastern outlets frame the veto as a necessary defense against Western pressure and the weaponization of international institutions, whereas Western reporting focuses on the impact of the veto on global sanctions enforcement.

item.title: United States Accuses Russian Intelligence Agents of Planning Assassinations of Dissidents Abroad
item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice unsealed charges against five individuals allegedly linked to Russian intelligence for conspiring to finance terrorism and murder-for-hire against dissidents and Ukrainian allies. Western outlets frame the story as a thwarted plot of Russian expansionism and a threat to international security. Conversely, Russian-aligned reporting focuses on the specific legal terminology of the indictment, highlighting the involvement of U.S. nationals and the mechanics of the American legal and intelligence apparatus.

item.title: Trump claims Ukraine and Russia have agreed to cease strikes on energy infrastructure.
item.description: How the same diplomatic maneuver is cast as a step toward de-escalation in the West and a provocative escalation in the East.
